<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9369, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

# Claude Sonnet 5.5

A fully local, Gmail-inspired mail client. No accounts, no network, no paid services. Everything lives in `localStorage`.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev        # http://127.0.0.1:9369
pnpm test       # unit tests (search engine, store actions, seed integrity)
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build && pnpm preview
pnpm e2e        # Playwright smoke suite against a running dev server (needs Chrome)
```

## What is in it

- Seeded mailbox of 90+ conversations: threads, attachments, calendar invites, promotions, receipts, spam, trash, drafts, a snoozed item, a scheduled send.
- Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Drafts, Scheduled, All Mail, Spam, Trash and user labels. Category tabs (Primary, Promotions, Social, Updates).
- Select, range-select, bulk archive / delete / spam / read / star / important / snooze / move / label, with undo for every action. Drag rows onto sidebar items and tabs.
- Search with Gmail-style operators (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `label:`, `has:attachment`, `is:unread`, `before:`, `after:`, `older_than:`, `larger:`, `in:anywhere`, quotes, `-` and `OR`), suggestions, recent searches, and an advanced filter form.
- Conversation view with collapsed history, quote trimming, message details, per-message actions, RSVP cards, attachment gallery with previews and downloads, smart replies, inline reply.
- Compose: contact autocomplete, Cc/Bcc, rich text, links, emoji, attachments (drag and drop too), autosaved drafts, undo send, schedule send, minimize / full screen / pop out. Contacts write back a few seconds after you send (toggle in settings).
- Keyboard shortcuts (`?` lists them), reading pane, density, light / dark / system themes, five accents, signature, page size, label manager, export and reset.
- Responsive: desktop, tablet drawer, and a mobile layout with full-screen compose, swipe to archive and long-press to select.

Data is versioned under the `sonnet-mail:v3` key. Use Settings > Data > Reset to restore the seed.

content.text:
Built. It's a local Gmail-style mail client titled "Claude Sonnet 5.5" (both `<title>` and the `h1`), and the dev server is up on port 9369.

Run it with `pnpm dev`. All checks pass:
- **Typecheck and build:** `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` are clean.
- **Unit tests:** 27 pass.
- **Playwright smoke suite:** 32 of 32 pass across desktop, tablet (820px) and mobile (390px).
- **Playwright deep suite:** 19 of 19 pass, run with `node e2e/deep.mjs`.
- **Page errors:** none in either suite.

Both Playwright suites need Chrome and a running dev server. `pnpm e2e` runs only the smoke suite.

What's in it:
- **Mailbox:** about 90 seeded conversations with threads, attachments, invites, drafts, snoozed and scheduled items.
- **Navigation:** Inbox, Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Drafts, Scheduled, All Mail, Spam, Trash, user labels and category tabs. Nothing is a placeholder.
- **Actions:** select, bulk actions, star, read/unread, archive, delete, label, snooze and drag-to-move. Every action has undo.
- **Search:** Gmail-style operators (`from:`, `label:`, `has:attachment`, `larger:` and so on), suggestions, recent searches and an advanced form.
- **Reading:** collapsed conversation history, per-message actions, RSVP cards, an attachment gallery with previews, and inline reply.
- **Compose:** contact autocomplete, Cc/Bcc, rich text and links, attachments, autosaved drafts, undo send and schedule send. Contacts reply a few seconds after you send, and you can turn that off in settings.
- **Settings and shortcuts:** shortcuts (press `?` for the list), reading pane, density, light/dark/system themes, five accents, signature, label manager, and export or reset of the data.
- **Layout:** drawer sidebar, full-screen compose and swipe or long-press on mobile.

This last round I checked the snooze menu, search panel, quick settings and schedule-send menu in screenshots and found no visual defects. I also made list rows keyboard-focusable and switched them to proper list semantics. I added `README.md` and `.gitignore` and removed the throwaway helper scripts.

I couldn't delete the `dist/` and `shots/` build and screenshot folders (the command was blocked), so they are still there. They are in `.gitignore`, so they're safe to remove by hand.Those background tasks (smoke suite runs, layout probe, dev server health, CPU check) finished successfully. They match what I already reported: 32 of 32 smoke tests, 19 of 19 deep tests, no page errors, and the dev server responding on port 9369. Nothing else to do.
